primary.title: The Edict of Milan
primary.author: Constantine the Great and Licinius
primary.rationale: This is a foundational document for religious tolerance in the Roman Empire, issued by Constantine and Licinius. While not a direct speech or letter from Constantine alone, it is directly attributed to his reign and policy.

primary.title: Letter to Eusebius of Caesarea
primary.author: Constantine the Great
primary.rationale: This letter, preserved in Eusebius's 'Life of Constantine,' details Constantine's instructions for the construction of churches in Constantinople and his theological views.

primary.title: Speeches (Oration to the Saints)
primary.author: Constantine the Great
primary.rationale: Though attribution is debated, these speeches are presented as Constantine's own in Eusebius's 'Life of Constantine,' reflecting his Christian beliefs and imperial authority.

secondary.title: Constantine the Great: Emperor, Christian, Revolutionary
secondary.author: Paul Stephenson
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive and well-regarded scholarly biography by a leading expert on the period, published by a major academic press.

secondary.title: The Cambridge Companion to the Age of Constantine
secondary.author: Noel Lenski
secondary.rationale: An edited volume featuring essays by numerous scholars covering various aspects of Constantine's reign and its impact, published by a prestigious university press.

secondary.title: Constantine's Conversion: Historical, Literary, and Theological Re-examinations
secondary.author: Paul J. Fedwick
secondary.rationale: An influential collection of essays that critically examines the traditional narrative of Constantine's conversion and its implications.

suggestions.notes: Primary source texts are often found within larger works by historians like Eusebius. Availability on digital archives is high, but direct, standalone texts can be rarer.
